messages:
maya: Heads-up — p99 latency on pool `gpu-shared-7` jumped ~3x around 11:30 UTC. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/perf/pools/gpu-shared-7 :eyes:
jamal: Any noisy tenant IDs yet?
oliver: I see a sustained burst from `tenant:mensa` at the same window, +increase in large-batch kernels. Quick sampling attached (snip): `kernel_switch -> aten_matmul_fast` spikes.
maya: attaching short `perf` dump and kv-stats from that node: ```
kv_cache.entries_total=124k
kv_cache.evictions=18k
avg_kv_hit=0.63
```
oliver: The kernel profile shows a switch to the slow matmul path when batch sizes > 48 and seq_len > 2048. Our autoswitch rule triggers and the kernel selection penalty kills tail latency.
sasha: So it's two things: batch heuristics pushing to an incompatible kernel + mensa's request pattern thrashing the KV cache?
jamal: Correct. mensa has many concurrent short chats + occasional long-sequence jobs. Their burst created oversized micro-batches that forced kernel path flip and caused KV churn.
maya: runtime-bot logged a config rollout at 11:28 for `batching.policy: aggressive` on that pool — could be related. runtime-bot: "deploy: batching-policy v2 applied to gpu-shared-7 by oliver at 11:27:50"
oliver: I rolled that earlier this morning to improve throughput for long-seq jobs, but didn't simulate mixed-tenancy bursts. My bad.
sasha: Immediate mitigation options?
jamal: 1) soft throttle `tenant:mensa` concurrency (token bucket) 2) revert aggressive batching on gpu-shared-7 3) move mensa to a burst-isolated pool if org agrees.
maya: Jamal, can you run a targeted throttle and monitor p99?
jamal: On it. Command: ```redwood ctl tenants throttle --id mensa --concurrency 8 --duration 20m```
jamal: Throttle applied. Monitoring now — p99 dropping back toward baseline within 90s :thumbsup:
oliver: I'll push a small change to batching config to add a max_batch_size cap for mixed tenants: snippet I propose: ```yaml
batching:
  policy: adaptive
  max_batch_size: 48
  consider_seq_len: true
```
sasha: Also let's add a per-tenant KV pin threshold to avoid eviction storms. Proposed follow-up: add telemetry for kernel_autoswitch events per-tenant and a fairness score.
maya: Agreed. Create follow-up ticket and assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml to tune kernels/batching.
jamal: Filing ticket now: https://redwood.internal/issue/ENG-4821 — summary: "gpu-shared-7: kernel flip + kv-eviction due to aggressive batching and mensa bursts"
oliver: Sorry for the rollout fallout. I'll revert the policy on that pool if we see any regression.
maya: Thanks everyone. Quick win confirmed — throttle helped. We'll work on longer-term config+telemetry changes. :white_check_mark:
